Title: Ridge model meets the documented historical evaluation checks
Description:

Scope: The listed local component/API checks; production observations are identified separately.

python -m pytest backend/tests/test_ridge_model.py -q
Check these inputs and results:
1. With the configured Ridge pipeline. Expected: The two steps are StandardScaler followed by Ridge with RIDGE_ALPHA.
2. With 200 seeded synthetic rows with the declared feature count. Expected: All 200 predictions are finite and have the expected one-dimensional shape.

4. With five-fold evaluation of the retained historical play-type dataset. Expected: Ridge mean RMSE is below the league-mean baseline RMSE.
5. With the earlier 80% of seasons for training and the remaining seasons for prediction. Expected: All predicted PPP values are between 0 and 2.5.
6. With five-fold evaluation of the retained historical dataset. Expected: Ridge RMSE is below 0.50 in each fold.
7. With the retained offense dataset and declared feature columns. Expected: X is two-dimensional with the declared feature count; y is one-dimensional; row counts match and all values are finite.
8. With the same 300 seeded synthetic rows with alpha 0.001, RIDGE_ALPHA and 10.0. Expected: Coefficient norms decrease strictly from the low alpha through the configured alpha to the high alpha.
Related cases: BST-88, BST-89, BST-90, BST-91, BST-92, BST-93, BST-94, BST-95.
Evidence: docs/assignment-1-revision/tests/backend-junit.xml and frontend-vitest.json.

Title: Top-K uplift matches possession-weighted calculations
Description:

4. Test zero or invalid denominators and too little usable data.
Expected: The values match the independent calculation within the stated tolerance, and the reference includes only the intended team and season. Invalid denominators produce a documented safe result or error. The result is clearly described as a historical modeled comparison, without claiming held-out accuracy or a proven improvement caused by the recommendations.
Comments:
I checked the uplift calculation with a worked example: a team average of 1.75 points per possession and 2.05 for the selected plays should give a +0.30 difference. The tests in [5092bf1](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/5092bf1d93ed7c30f2e2b7b34eddd613f4ece474) returned that result and still used the full team-season average when only one play was selected.
The tests also kept teams and seasons separate and handled negative differences, zero averages and unusable data correctly. BST-127/128 still need live testing; this historical comparison does not prove the plays will improve future results.

The uplift calculation passed on the live backend from [e950869](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/e950869cb318c6b44220d3c06be4ba2aa16521da).
The independent example matched +0.30 PPP, with team/season separation and invalid-data checks passing.
For TOR vs BOS in 2024-25 with three plays, JSON and CSV both showed 0.969238 team-average PPP, 1.071696 modeled PPP and a 0.102458 difference.
Results are in live-verification.json; these are historical comparisons, not proof of actual or future improvement.

The Top-K tests passed again, including independently calculated possession-weighted PPP, the team-season reference, negative uplift, zero denominators and invalid input. Changes to other teams and seasons do not enter the selected reference.

Comments:
The coach and analyst browser tests were still pending.
The local tests passed, but I still needed working test accounts and the new deployment before checking real sign-in, allowed pages, blocked pages and the main workflows.
The next update would record what actually worked or failed in the browser.

Export CSV failed with “Invalid or missing session token.”
I recorded the problem in BST-129 and SCRUM-527, so this browser test was still incomplete.

Title: Signed-in browser downloads preserve authorization
Description:
Covers [SCRUM-527](https://basketball-strategy.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-527) under SCRUM-506.
Before testing: Use the deployed frontend/backend, a signed-in account with the required role, and a loaded dataset.
Steps:
1. As an analyst, export the main and filtered Data Explorer CSVs, then check the saved filenames, headers and rows.
2. Export a CSV from Shot Explorer.
3. Check that protected download requests use the current session’s authorization token.
4. Test a denied or expired session: the page should show a useful error, stop its busy indicator and avoid saving the error response as a file.
5. Check the existing baseline CSV and shot PDF with the appropriate role and record what happens.
Expected: Allowed exports save with the correct content, filenames and authorization. Unauthorized requests show an error and do not create a downloaded file.
The first export test failed. A signed-in analyst saw 11 TOR offense rows, but Export CSV opened Cloud Run with “Invalid or missing session token.” The comments show the fixes, later failures and final saved-file retest.
Comments:
The live Data Explorer export test failed.
I signed in as an analyst and loaded 11 TOR offense rows, but Export CSV opened the backend page with “Invalid or missing session token” because the download link did not send the login token.
I started the fix in SCRUM-527 and added baseline CSV and shot PDF to the review list; those two exports had not yet been confirmed as failures.

Five local download tests passed, covering the login token, exact CSV content and filename, PDF filenames, a CSV filename fallback, cleanup after a click error, and a rejected 403 response without a downloaded file.
All 17 frontend tests and TypeScript also passed, using mocked sessions and responses.
The fix still needed deployment and a signed-in browser retest.
A coach baseline export click timed out while waiting for a download, so that result was inconclusive and this case stayed open.

The browser retest failed after 1068ef2 deployed.
Export CSV now created a Downloads entry, but it showed Stopped, which I confirmed in the browser.
The 17 local tests and API checks passed, but the file still was not saving, so SCRUM-527 stayed In Progress.
I planned to route downloads through the app so the browser could save an authenticated file normally.

The download retest passed on the [live app](https://nbaplayranker-seven.vercel.app) after c3044da routed downloads through the app.
I checked newly saved Data Explorer and Shot Explorer CSVs and a readable TOR/BOS shot-plan PDF; the Data Explorer CSV finished and opened.
Live checks confirmed correct files and blocked unauthorized requests without downloading errors as files.
Results are in downloaded-file-verification.json and export-proxy-live-verification.json; local tests and the build passed, but a separate coach file saving through a browser click was not confirmed here.

I found one missed download route: the coach Matchup PDF at /export/playtype-viz.pdf was not allowed through the new download route.
I reopened this case as Fail until that PDF route was added and retested, keeping SCRUM-527 and SCRUM-506 In Progress.
The Data Explorer CSV, Shot Explorer CSV and shot-plan PDF saves above still passed, but they did not test this separate coach PDF.

The final download retest passed after [18baffc](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/18baffc0cc6f99273f60e797a499804029b8b84f) added the missing coach PDF route to the [live app](https://nbaplayranker-seven.vercel.app), and [GitHub checks](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/actions/runs/37157802665) passed.
I checked newly saved analyst CSVs, the coach baseline CSV, and both shot-plan and coach play-type PDFs for correct content.
Live checks also confirmed that unauthorized downloads were blocked.
Results are in downloaded-file-verification.json and export-proxy-live-verification.json; this resolved the missed coach PDF route and the earlier missing-token and Stopped-download problems.

Description:

Expected result: no failed requests, peak process memory below the 2048 MB Cloud Run limit, memory growth under 200 MB, p95 latency under 2 s.
Comments:
Executed 2026-10-03 on main (commit 120a5d3), Windows 11, Python 3.14: 1 passed. 400 requests from 8 concurrent users, 0 errors, 138 requests/s, latency p50 61 ms / p95 77 ms / max 84 ms, process memory 306 MB before and 308 MB peak. Result: Pass. Caveat: en_core_web_sm was not installed locally, so the pipeline used its spacy.blank fallback; the trained model footprint and the deployed Cloud Run service are not covered by this run.

The local NLP load test completed 400 requests from eight concurrent users with no errors. Its p95 latency was 333.1 ms and peak process memory was 299.3 MiB, both within the test limits. This result covers the local process.

Title: Shot import keeps the event team separate from home team and score
Description:
Covers UC63 Compute Aggregates; UC70 Get accurate shot type predictions using an appropriate model.
Related work: [SCRUM-479](https://basketball-strategy.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-479).
Steps:
1. Create two synthetic shot events in one TOR/BOS game, one from each shooting-team ID.
2. Include home-team and away-team abbreviations and a numeric home score, but no shooting-team abbreviation or home flag.
3. Run build_shots_clean once with home_score 0 and once with home_score 42.
4. Compare team, opponent and home/away flag against the independently specified shooter IDs.
Expected result: The TOR event maps to TOR/BOS/home and the BOS event to BOS/TOR/away, regardless of the home score.
Comments:
Both score variants misattribute the shooting teams. This proves a current ETL defect on a representative schema; it does not prove the historical raw schema.
Fix: [SCRUM-538](https://basketball-strategy.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-538).
Evidence: [shot-attribution-junit.xml](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/main/docs/assignment-1-revision/tests/shot-attribution-junit.xml), [shot-attribution.log](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/main/docs/assignment-1-revision/tests/shot-attribution.log).
